note: Independent re-judgment against RFC 4271 Section 5 ("If a path with a recognized, transitive optional attribute is accepted and passed along to other BGP peers and the Partial bit in the Attribute Flags octet is set to 1 by some previous AS, it MUST NOT be set back to 0 by the current AS."). Positive: TestRFC4271PartialFromPreviousASNotCleared and TestRFC4271PartialFromPreviousASNeverCleared prove ingress walk and enforceRFC7606 -> publishBase preserve 0xE0 on recognized COMMUNITIES; TestReceivedPartialSurvivesOrdinarySessionWire proves ordinary eBGP->RIB->iBGP Session wire and destination reconnect replay retain Partial=1 on all four dedicated pooled optional-transitive attributes (AGGREGATOR, COMMUNITY, EXTENDED_COMMUNITY, LARGE_COMMUNITY); TestAggregatorPartialSurvivesASPathRebuild and TestPrefixSIDPartialSurvivesNextHopCleanup prove automatic AS-width AGGREGATOR rebuild (genericAttrSetHandler) and next-hop Prefix-SID cleanup (prefixSIDNextHopHandler) preserve received Partial=1. Negative: TestRFC4271CompleteRecognizedTransitiveStaysClearOnSessionWire proves recognized optional transitive attributes received with Partial=0 stay 0xC0 in RIB storage, Session wire, and reconnect replay (conditioning preservation on received Partial via pooledTransitiveFlags); TestRFC4271PartialClearedOutsideOptionalTransitiveOnRelayedWire proves well-known ORIGIN (0x60) and optional non-transitive MED (0xA0) have Partial actively cleared to 0x40 and 0x80 on publishBase -> route-server relay wire (ClearPartialOnWellKnownAndNonTransitive), resolving the prior missing-negative weak finding. All 7 tagged units carry fresh discrimination records.
